objective: Improve geometric-mean mimalloc operations per second on four frozen deterministic single-thread, four-thread, small-object, and fragmentation workloads. The pinned upstream api/api-fill/stress suite, deterministic checksums, a four-thread maximum, peak allocator page-committed bytes, and live-page fragmentation at or below the split baseline plus 1% are hard gates. Only allocator implementation files under src and internal headers under include/mimalloc are mutable; trusted statistics and all build, test, evaluator, and workload code are protected.

meta.provenance: microsoft/mimalloc at exact revision 76d3f8a934f9761e4ee75fa8b071e58d482f2758; four independently authored protected C workload drivers use sealed deterministic xorshift64-v1 seeds over a fixed per-workload round budget; terminal holdout received no optimizer, mutation, or headroom pilot; native AMD64 terminal ordering and rebaseline evidence is recorded at diagnostics/native-amd64-rebaseline.json.

mutableEnvelope: src/** except src/stats.c, src/static.c, and src/alloc-override.c

definition.deviationFromPriorFreeze: container-build definition only: immutable native AMD64 base, dependency pins, complete filesystem timestamp normalization, and deterministic bind-mounted license installation; capsule source, evaluator, objective, assets, and baseline were unchanged

measurement.q: geometric mean over four drivers of the load-cancelling yardstick score sealed_operations * (min reference elapsed / min candidate elapsed)
measurement.benchmarkSampleSelection: per workload the candidate and the pristine reference are timed interleaved (7 samples each) and scored q = sealed operations * (min reference elapsed / min candidate elapsed); the trusted evaluator times each measured region with its own monotonic clock across a per-sample fresh-nonce handshake, so candidate code can neither observe nor fabricate the measurement, the per-binary minimum rejects scheduler-noise outliers, and the reference ratio cancels sustained per-eval host load
measurement.peakCommittedGate: for each workload, mi_stats_get page_committed.peak after a fresh mi_stats_reset and fixed one-round memory pass must be <= split baseline * 1.01
measurement.fragmentationGate: at each driver's fixed live allocation checkpoint, max(0,page_committed.current-(malloc_normal.current+malloc_huge.current))/page_committed.current from merged mi_stats must be <= split baseline * 1.01
measurement.workBudget: each workload runs a fixed sealed round budget; expectedOperations is the deterministic (allocator-independent) operation count for that budget and is validated against every reported sample
measurement.treePeakGate: kernel cgroup whole-tree memory.peak per workload must be <= split baseline * 1.20 (regression ceiling) AND >= split baseline * 0.25 (workload floor: a completion stream produced without running the allocator is rejected)
measurement.referenceYardstick: each workload builds a pristine reference (the sealed baseline allocator from TRUSTED_DIR with no candidate overlay) and times reference and candidate interleaved under the same host load; the score is q = sealed operations * (min reference elapsed / min candidate elapsed), so sustained per-eval contention elevates both legs together and cancels in the ratio

exploitReview.protectedPathEscape: broker diff-protects build files, public/statistics headers, statistics implementation, evaluator, worker, tests, and four workload drivers; evaluator rejects symlinks and new files outside src or include/mimalloc
exploitReview.benchmarkSpecialCasing: distinct sealed train and validation seeds; a trusted first-size fingerprint diagnostic is expected to win train and lose validation
exploitReview.fixtureFingerprinting: both split configurations are holdout-only and mounted under root-owned /capsule; compilation runs as uid 2000 before the protected evaluator invokes drivers
exploitReview.outputFabrication: the trusted evaluator owns fd 1 and never scores anything the candidate-linked executable prints; the benchmark streams only work-completion tokens over a parent-supplied report fd, authenticated per sample by a fresh unpredictable nonce, and the parent measures elapsed with its own monotonic clock, derives throughput from the sealed operation count, and validates the deterministic checksum. A constructor that skips the workload cannot write the scoring channel, cannot fabricate the parent clock, and (via the whole-tree cgroup memory floor) cannot reproduce the sealed memory profile without allocating; the evaluator additionally audits every linked binary with nm and rejects candidate-defined timing or output symbols
exploitReview.buildScriptMutation: CMake files, fixed O2/MI_STAT flags, worker, test sources, and toolchain lock are protected; every evaluation performs a clean source rebuild
exploitReview.timerTampering: the candidate-linked benchmark performs no scored timing of its own: the trusted evaluator process brackets each measured region with its own CLOCK_MONOTONIC across a per-sample authenticated handshake the child cannot pre-answer, runs under uid 2000 with network disabled, and the nm symbol audit still rejects any candidate-defined timing or output symbols before a benchmark binary is executed
exploitReview.deadCodeBenchmarkBypass: the benchmark uses public allocation entry points linked to the same static library exercised by upstream api and stress tests
